subject: Anthropology
title: Value Theory
description: A quick, practical guide to Value Theory.

hook.text: A diamond costs more than water, but water keeps you alive. Why do we value rare things over essential ones?

buildup.text: Anthropologists ask what makes things valuable. Is it labor, scarcity, demand, or social meaning that creates value?

discovery.text: Marx said value comes from labor. Simmel said it comes from desire and distance. Each theory reveals different truths.

twist.text: Value isn't just economic. A family heirloom is worthless at auction but priceless to its owner. Context creates value.

climax.text: Value is always relational. Nothing has value in isolation — only in a web of social relationships and cultural meaning.

punchline.text: Value is created by people, not inherent in things.

quiz.question: Where does value come from according to anthropology?
options: From social relationships, labor, desire, and cultural meaning

details.summary: Value theory in economic anthropology asks what people consider valuable and how value is created. Unlike economics, which reduces value to price, anthropological value theory explores how cultural meanings, social labor, and moral frameworks create different systems of valuation across cultures.
details.whyItMatters: Value theory reveals that price and worth are not the same thing. Understanding how different cultures create and measure value challenges market pricing as the only legitimate valuation system and raises questions about what is truly valuable in.
takeaways: Value theory asks what people consider valuable and how value is created
It goes beyond market price to examine cultural and moral valuation
Different cultures create fundamentally different systems of value

faq.question: How does anthropological value theory differ from economic value theory?
faq.answer: Economics reduces value to market price determined by supply and demand. Anthropological value theory examines how labor, social relationships, cultural meaning, and moral frameworks create multiple forms of value that cannot be reduced to monetary equivalents.

faq.question: What did David Graeber contribute to value theory?
faq.answer: Graeber proposed that value is the importance of action — the way people invest effort, creativity, and meaning in what they do. This definition links value to human agency and cultural priorities rather than market mechanisms, reuniting economic and cultural analysis.
